items.title: Stationary thermal geometric data
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], and let
$\nabla$ be its unique torsion-free $g$-compatible connection supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix a nonempty
connected open set $O\subseteq M$. A **selected stationary thermal carrier** on
$O$ consists of a smooth future timelike vector field $\xi$ and a smooth
positive scalar field $T:O\to(0,\infty)$, where $T$ is measured in kelvins,
such that $\xi$ is a Killing field of $g$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-killing-field]]. Equivalently, the criterion is
$\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$ by
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]. The round brackets mean
symmetrization with factor $1/2$. The choice of $\xi$ specifies the thermal congruence; no
coordinate chart or universal observer field is selected.

Set $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and $u:=\xi/N_\xi$. Then
$g(u,u)=-1$. In the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$, $u$ is
dimensionless and $cu$ is the physical four-velocity, with $c>0$ in
$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For a fixed Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in
$\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, define the inverse-temperature vector
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and the Killing-normalized
temperature field $T_K:=N_\xi T$. Thus $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$; this definition
does not assert that $T_K$ is constant.

For a smooth chemical-potential scalar $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ in joules, put
$\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$, a dimensionless scalar. Define the rest-space metric,
derivative, acceleration, expansion and shear by
$$h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_au_b,\qquad D:=u^a\nabla_a,\qquad a_b:=u^a\nabla_au_b,\qquad \theta:=\nabla_au^a,\qquad \sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac13\theta h_{ab}.$$
Here $a$, $\theta$ and $\sigma$ have inverse-length units; the physical
proper acceleration is $c^2a$. The smooth tangent-bundle structure used by
the cited GR suppliers assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]]; no stronger choice principle is part of this
definition.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §§III.3 and VI.2
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.2.3 and 4.3.1
José Santiago and Matt Visser, Tolman-like temperature gradients in stationary spacetimes, §§III–V

items.title: Canonical future massive mass-shell measure
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], let $x\in M$, and let
$M_*>0$ be a rest-energy parameter in joules. The **future massive shell at
$x$** is the Borel subset
$$\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}:=\{P\in T_xM:g_x(P,P)=-M_*^2,\ P\text{ future-directed}\}.$$
Use any smooth future orthonormal tetrad near $x$, whose existence is
[[thm-gr-local-lorentz-tetrad-existence]]. At $x$ write its basis as
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and, for $q=(q_1,q_2,q_3)\in\mathbb R^3$ with energy
coordinates in joules, put
$$E(q):=\sqrt{M_*^2+|q|^2},\qquad P_e(q):=E(q)e_0+\sum_{i=1}^3q_i e_i.$$
Let $\lambda_3$ be Euclidean Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]],
[[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]]). For every Borel set
$A\subseteq\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$, with its subspace Borel sigma-algebra
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), define
$$\mu_{M_*,x,e}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf1_A(P_e(q))\,\frac{1}{E(q)}\,d\lambda_3(q).$$
In these tetrad coordinates the shell equation is
$-(P^0)^2+|q|^2=-M_*^2$, and the future sheet has $P^0>0$, hence
$P^0=E(q)$. Thus $P_e$ is a bijection onto the shell with continuous inverse
$q_i=g(P,e_i)$, so it is a homeomorphism. Continuous preimages of Borel sets are Borel
([[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]), and
$1/E(q)$ is a positive continuous density. The nonnegative Lebesgue integral
over a measurable set is [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]; the
positive-density measure theorem [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]] makes
$\mu_{M_*,x,e}$ a positive Borel measure. Its coordinate expression is
$d^3q/E(q)$ and its units are $\mathrm{J^2}$.

Theorem [[lem-tgr-mass-shell-measure-tetrad-invariance]] proves that this
measure is independent of the chosen future orthonormal tetrad. We therefore
write it as $\mu_{M_*,x}$, or $d\mu_{M_*}$ when the fiber is understood. The
underlying Lebesgue and tetrad suppliers use $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ exactly as
declared by [[def-countable-choice]]; no arbitrary-index choice is asserted.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §§II and III.3
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.3.3 and 4.3.1

items.title: Killing temperature normalization and rigidity
items.statement:
Let $O$ and the smooth fields $(g,\nabla,\xi,T,u,N_\xi,\beta)$ be as in
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]. Then
$$\beta\text{ is Killing}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\xi T=T_K\text{ for a constant }T_K>0.$$
When this holds, $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$, and the Killing congruence has
$$\xi(N_\xi)=0,\qquad a=\nabla\log N_\xi,\qquad \theta=0,\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0.$$
If $\xi$ is replaced by $b\xi$ with a constant $b>0$, then
$N_\xi$ and $T_K$ scale by $b$, while $u$ and $\beta$ are unchanged.

references.title: José Santiago and Matt Visser, Tolman-like temperature gradients in stationary spacetimes, §§III–V
Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §VI.2
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.2.3 and 4.3.1

items.title: Exact thermal Killing kinematic equivalence
items.statement:
Let $O$ be a connected open set in a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold, let $u$ be a smooth future unit timelike vector field on $O$
($g(u,u)=-1$), and let $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth. Define
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$, $h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_au_b$,
$D:=u^a\nabla_a$, $a_b:=u^a\nabla_au_b$,
$\theta:=\nabla_au^a$ and
$\sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\theta h_{ab}/3$ as in
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]. Then $\beta$ is a Killing field of
$g$ (equivalently $\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=0$ by
[[def-gr-killing-field]] and
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]) if and only if
$$DT=0,\qquad \theta=0,\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0,\qquad h_a{}^b\nabla_b\log T=-a_a.$$
No hypersurface-orthogonality or vanishing-vorticity condition is assumed.

references.title: José Santiago and Matt Visser, Tolman-like temperature gradients in stationary spacetimes, §§II–V
Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §VI.2

items.title: Natural tensors under Killing isometries
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], let $O\subseteq M$ be open, and let
$\xi$ be a smooth nowhere-zero vector field on $O$ satisfying
$\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$ for the unique metric-selected connection $\nabla$
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Its local flow
$\Phi_s$ exists on the open flow
domains supplied by [[thm-flow-box-theorem]]. On every common flow domain,
$\Phi_s$ is a local isometry and preserves $\nabla$ and $\xi$. Consequently
it preserves the curvature tensor $R$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]], all finite covariant
derivatives of $R$ and $\xi$, and every tensor or scalar obtained from these
fields by finitely many tensor products, contractions, and smooth scalar
operations. The assertion is local; it assumes no complete flow or global
isometry group. It makes no claim about arbitrary quantum observables or their
analytic representation by local curvature data.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.2.3, 2.3.3 and 4.3.1
Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §VI.2

items.title: Mass-shell polynomial rigidity
items.statement:
Let $(V,g,C^+)$ be a four-dimensional time-oriented Lorentz vector space of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with future cone $C^+$ as in
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]. Let $M>0$ and let $A$ be a
symmetric bilinear form on $V$ and $b$ a covector. If
$$A(P,P)+b(P)=0\qquad\text{for every }P\in C^+\text{ with }g(P,P)=-M^2,$$
then $A=0$ and $b=0$. If instead this identity holds for every nonzero future
null vector $P\in\overline{C^+}$, then $b=0$ and $A=\lambda g$ for some
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$. The second clause is the exact massless conformal
exception.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §§III.3 and VI.2
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.1–2.2 and 4.3.1

items.title: Tetrad invariance of the future massive mass-shell measure
items.statement:
Let $x$ be an event of a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$M_*>0$, and let $e$ and $e'$ be any two smooth future orthonormal tetrads
near $x$. The measures $d\mu_{M_*,x,e}$ and $d\mu_{M_*,x,e'}$ defined in
[[def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure]] agree on every Borel subset of the future
massive shell at $x$. Hence the fiber measure $d\mu_{M_*,x}$ is independent of
the chosen future orthonormal tetrad.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §§II and III.3
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.3.3 and 4.3.1

items.title: Jüttner partition, probability, and perfect-fluid moments
items.statement:
Let $x$ be an event in a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$M_*>0$ be an energy in joules, and let $u\in T_xM$ be future unit timelike,
$g(u,u)=-1$. Fix $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $T>0$ in kelvins,
$n>0$ in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, $c>0$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and a reference
action $h_{\rm ref}>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Put
$$\alpha:=\frac1{k_BT},\qquad \beta:=\frac{u}{k_BT},\qquad E_u(P):=-g(P,u).$$
For $j=0,1,2,3$ and $z>0$ define
$$K_j(z):=\int_0^\infty e^{-z\cosh t}\cosh(jt)\,dt.$$
With the future-shell measure of [[def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure]], define
$$I_{M_*}(\alpha):=\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}e^{g(\beta,P)}\,d\mu_{M_*}(P),\qquad Z_{M_*}(\alpha):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-\alpha E(q)}\,d^3q,$$
where $E(q)=\sqrt{M_*^2+|q|^2}$ in a future orthonormal tetrad whose time
axis is $u$. Both integrals are finite and positive, and
$$I_{M_*}(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi M_*}{\alpha}K_1(\alpha M_*),\qquad Z_{M_*}(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi M_*^2}{\alpha}K_2(\alpha M_*).$$
The observer-rest momentum law
$$d\nu_u(q):=Z_{M_*}(\alpha)^{-1}e^{-\alpha E(q)}d^3q$$
is a probability measure. Define the dimensionless occupation and its number
current and stress moments by
$$\zeta:=\log\!\left(\frac{n h_{\rm ref}^3c^3}{Z_{M_*}(\alpha)}\right),\qquad f(P):=e^{\zeta+g(\beta,P)},$$
$$J^a:=(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}P^a f(P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P),\qquad T^{ab}:=(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}P^aP^b f(P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P).$$
These integrals converge, and, with
$$\varepsilon:=n\left(M_*\frac{K_1(\alpha M_*)}{K_2(\alpha M_*)}+\frac3\alpha\right),\qquad p:=\frac n\alpha=nk_BT,$$
they satisfy $J^a=nu^a$ and
$T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+p)u^au^b+pg^{ab}$. The quantities $J$ and $T$ have
units $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$ and $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, respectively. The reference
action $h_{\rm ref}$ is only a declared phase-space unit convention; it is
not Planck's constant or a measured parameter.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §III.3
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §4.3.1

items.title: Massive Jüttner stationarity and normalization
items.statement:
Let $O$ be a connected open subset of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let $M_*>0$ be a
rest-energy, let $\beta$ be a smooth vector field with units
$\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, let $\zeta:O\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and dimensionless, and
define on the future massive shell
$$f(x,P):=\exp\bigl(\zeta(x)+g_x(\beta(x),P)\bigr),\qquad \mathcal L:=P^a\frac{\partial}{\partial x^a}-\Gamma^a{}_{bc}P^bP^c\frac{\partial}{\partial P^a}.$$
The geodesic Liouville vector field $\mathcal L$ is tangent to
$\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$ and
$$\mathcal Lf=0\text{ on every future massive shell} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=0\text{ and }d\zeta=0,$$
where $\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=0$ is the covariant Killing condition
([[def-gr-killing-field]], [[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]).
Since $O$ is connected, $d\zeta=0$ means $\zeta$ is constant on $O$.

For any vector $\beta_x\in T_xM$, define its shell normalizer by
$$I_{M_*}(\beta_x):=\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}e^{g_x(\beta_x,P)}\,d\mu_{M_*,x}(P).$$
This integral is finite exactly when $\beta_x$ is future timelike. If so, with
$\alpha:=\sqrt{-g_x(\beta_x,\beta_x)}>0$, it equals
$4\pi M_*K_1(\alpha M_*)/\alpha$ as in
[[thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments]]. In particular, for carrier data
$\beta=u/(k_BT)$, the choice
$$\zeta=\log\!\left(\frac{n h_{\rm ref}^3c^3}{Z_{M_*}(1/(k_BT))}\right)$$
normalizes the proper number density to $n$ and gives exactly the number
current and stress moments of
[[thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments]]. This is a mathematical theorem about
the specified exponential ansatz; it does not assert that a material
thermalizes or that a physical equilibrium state exists.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §§III.3 and VI.2
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §4.3.1
José Santiago and Matt Visser, Tolman-like temperature gradients in stationary spacetimes, §IV

items.title: No massive Killing equilibrium in a spatially flat expanding FLRW metric
items.statement:
Let $L_0>0$ be a length and take
$O=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^3$ with coordinates $(s,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, where
$s$ and $x^i$ have length units. Give $O$ the time-oriented Lorentzian metric
of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
$$g=-ds^2+a(s)^2\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j,\qquad a(s):=s/L_0,$$
with future direction increasing $s$. This is the spatially flat FLRW
geometry with the scale factor explicitly fixed to $a(s)=s/L_0$.

(a) The scalar curvature, using the convention of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]], is $S(s)=6/s^2$. Consequently
no nonempty open subset of $O$ admits a timelike Killing vector field.

(b) By [[thm-tgr-massive-juttner-stationarity]], the specified normalizable
massive exponential ansatz has no stationary state on any nonempty open
subset of $O$.

(c) On the future null shell, the exponential transport condition instead
permits conformal Killing inverse-temperature fields. In particular,
$\beta=b(s/L_0)\partial_s$ for a constant $b>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$ is future
timelike and conformal Killing, and for constant $\zeta$ the massless
exponential $f=e^{\zeta+g(\beta,P)}$ satisfies the null-shell Liouville
equation. This is a mathematical null-shell example; it asserts no physical
state or empirical radiation result.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §VIII
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §4.3.1
